question: How many shade balls must be trapped under you to keep you above water?
answer: Each shade ball is almost half full of water, so underwater it holds up only about 300 g. It takes more than 260 of them, about 78 kg, to lift a person clear. The page asks how many must be trapped under the swimmer, and you drag shade balls under them to find out.
move: A shade ball lifts only ~300 g, so standing on them takes 260+.

web.label: Interactive page asking how many floating shade balls must be trapped under a swimmer to keep them above water, with a drag control to trap balls under the swimmer.

source: Veritasium, “Can You Swim in Shade Balls?” (YouTube, 2019)
